previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of coronary artery disease, prior CABG, diabetes, and hypertension was readmitted within 24 hours of discharge due to persistent left shoulder pain, constipation, and abdominal discomfort. She had recently fallen and sustained a musculoskeletal injury when her arm was grabbed. Serial troponins were negative, with no EKG changes, ruling out acute cardiac injury. Pain was reproducible on exam, supporting a musculoskeletal origin. Constipation was managed with bowel regimen adjustments. She remained stable on telemetry, continued her baseline cardiac and diabetes medications, and was discharged home with a short-term pain prescription and follow-up appointments in primary care and cardiology, including a scheduled stress test.

Brief Hospital Course:
Assessment and Plan: ___ y/o female with recent NSTEMI and 
atypical chest pain admitted with chest pain with probable 
costochondritis, and negative cardiac enzymes and a negative 
stress test, but with an elevated ESR.
. 
# Costochondritis. The patient presented to the ED with 
hypertensive emergency with an elevated blood pressure.  She had 
chest pain at that time and was started on a nitro gtt, but she 
was not bolused with heparin.  Her cardiac enzymes were negative 
and her ECG did not demonstrate ST segment or T wave changes 
suggestive of an ACS. She was ruled out for ACS with two 
negative enzymes and she underwent a stress test, which did not 
reproduce any anginal symptoms.  Of note, her exam was 
consistent with costochondritis, and she had very point 
tenderness across the L side of the precordium.  This tenderness 
diminished significantly prior to discharge.   She did not have 
ECG changes or PE findings consistent with pericarditis.  She 
was discharged with an ACE inhibiter, Beta-blocker, and Imdur as 
well as sublingual nitroglycerin.  She has a follow up with her 
cardiologist in early ___.
- Day Care: Please make sure Ms. ___ has transportation to 
her cardiology appointment.
.
# Elevated ESR/CRP: She had a markedly elevated ESR and CRP.  
She has had chronic headaches, and had a complaint of blurry 
vision associated with these headaches.  These headaches however 
have been going on for the past year.  She did not have any 
temporal tenderness, in addition to the absence of any focal 
neurological findings.  She will need outpatient follow up to 
determine the etiology of the elevated enzymes.
- Day Care: Please transport patient to her next PCP appointment 
with ___ on ___.
.
# Constipation: Upon admission she was passing gas and had a 
recent bowel movement.  There was palpable stool in the 
transverse colon.  She was given Mag Citrate and had several 
bowel movements.  She was discharged home on daily MiraLax in 
addition to senna and Colace. 
.  
# Diabetes: Her blood sugar remains elevated despite an insulin 
sliding scale.  Her metformin was held while she was admitted 
due to concern she may require a cardiac catheterization.

appointment the ___ is listed in her page 1.
.

at goal.  Her statin was increased, she was started on fish oil, 
and her niacin was discontinued.

# Asthma: No acute exacerbation while she was admitted.  She was 
continued on her home medications.  
.  
# Benign Essential Hypertension:  She was hypertensive while she 
was admitted and she presented with hypertensive emergency.  Her 
metoprolol was increased in addition to her amlodipine.

# Chronic Medical Problems: Depression/Anxiety, Anemia and GERD
